claim: A doxycycline-inducible adipose tissue-specific ANG-2 overexpression mouse model was generated by crossing TRE-ANG2 transgenic mice with adiponectin promoter-driven rtTA transgenic mice (Adipo-rtTA).
source: To directly evaluate the role of ANG-2 in AT, we took advantage of a mouse model carrying a tetracycline responsive element (TRE)-driven ANG-2 transgenic cassette (TRE-ANG2), shown schematically in Figure 1A. To obtain adipocyte-specific overexpression, we used a reverse tetracycline-dependent transcriptional activator (rtTA) which is driven by the adiponectin promoter (Adipo-rtTA). rtTA can bind and activate the TRE in the presence of Dox. Thus, we obtained the double transgenic mouse model (Adipo-ANG2) by crossing the TRE-ANG2 mice to the Adipo-rtTA mice and achieved an inducible and tissue-specific overexpression model of ANG-2 in the AT.
evidence: The manuscript describes the generation of the mouse model through breeding and genetic manipulation.

claim: After 5 weeks of Dox feeding, both subcutaneous and epididymal WAT show a significant increase in Angpt2 transcription in Adipo-ANG2 mice compared to control mice.
source: After 5 weeks of Dox feeding, we harvested different fat pads and other tissues from both Adipo-ANG2 and Adipo-rtTA mice (serving as controls) and assessed Angpt2 mRNA levels. While both subcutaneous and epididymal WAT (sWAT and eWAT, respectively) show a significant increase in Angpt2 transcription, there was no elevation of Angpt2 mRNA levels in the liver, kidney or heart (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1B demonstrating increased Angpt2 mRNA in adipose tissues.

claim: There was no elevation of Angpt2 mRNA levels in the liver, kidney or heart of Adipo-ANG2 mice after Dox induction.
source: While both subcutaneous and epididymal WAT (sWAT and eWAT, respectively) show a significant increase in Angpt2 transcription, there was no elevation of Angpt2 mRNA levels in the liver, kidney or heart (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data in Figure 1B showing tissue-specific expression.

claim: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) shows enhancement of Angpt2 transcription in Adipo-ANG2 mice.
source: Notably, we also noticed enhancement of Angpt2 transcription in brown adipose tissue (BAT).
evidence: The manuscript reports observing increased Angpt2 mRNA in BAT.

claim: Subcutaneous WAT shows the most abundant expression of Angpt2 mRNA among adipose tissues in Adipo-ANG2 mice.
source: Since the most abundant expression of Angpt2 mRNA was observed in sWAT, we examined the protein levels of ANG-2 in sWAT by Western blotting.
evidence: The manuscript states that sWAT had the highest Angpt2 mRNA expression based on their measurements.

claim: ANG-2 protein levels are significantly elevated in sWAT of Adipo-ANG2 transgenic mice compared to Adipo-rtTA control mice.
source: Compared to Adipo-rtTA control mice, ANG-2 protein levels are significantly elevated in Adipo-ANG2 transgenic mice (Figure 1C).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 1C demonstrates increased ANG-2 protein.

claim: Immunofluorescence staining reveals substantially higher ANG-2 signal in sWAT of Adipo-ANG2 mice compared to control mice.
source: In addition, immunofluorescence staining of ANG-2 in sWAT reveals a substantially higher ANG-2 signal in Adipo-ANG2 mice (Figure 1D).
evidence: Immunofluorescence imaging in Figure 1D shows increased ANG-2 staining.

claim: Vegfa, Tek (TIE2), Pecam1 (CD31), and Antxr1 (TEM8) are all significantly up-regulated in sWAT of Adipo-ANG2 transgenic mice after 5 weeks of HFD/Dox feeding.
source: After the mice were subjected to HFD/Dox containing diet for five weeks, a number of endothelial and angiogenic markers were assessed by qPCR in sWAT of both Adipo-rtTA control mice and Adipo-ANG2 mice. Vegfa, the angiopoietin receptor TIE2 (gene name Tek), the endothelial marker CD31 (Pecam1 as the gene name) and the angiogenesis marker tumor endothelial marker-8 (TEM8, Antxr1) are all significantly up-regulated in Adipo-ANG2 transgenic mice, indicating that the local angiogenic program is activated upon ANG-2 induction (Figure 2A).
evidence: qPCR data in Figure 2A shows upregulation of these angiogenic markers.

claim: Vascular density in sWAT is dramatically increased in Adipo-ANG2 transgenic mice as demonstrated by endomucin immunostaining.
source: In addition, the vascular density of sWAT was determined by immunostaining with antibodies to an additional endothelial marker, endomucin (Liu et al., 2001) (Figure 2B) with a quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2C. This reveals dramatically increased vascular density in Adipo-ANG2 transgenic mice.
evidence: Immunostaining and quantification in Figures 2B and 2C demonstrate increased vascular density.

claim: HIF-1α protein and gene expression levels are significantly decreased in sWAT of ANG-2 transgenic mice.
source: We observe a significant decrease in hypoxia inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) protein and gene expression levels, as well as a significant reduction in the expression levels of the HIF-1α downstream target gene Slc2a1 (gene symbol for GLUT1) in ANG-2 transgenic mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Western blot and qPCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-C show decreased HIF-1α.

claim: Slc2a1 (GLUT1) expression levels are significantly reduced in sWAT of ANG-2 transgenic mice.
source: We observe a significant decrease in hypoxia inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) protein and gene expression levels, as well as a significant reduction in the expression levels of the HIF-1α downstream target gene Slc2a1 (gene symbol for GLUT1) in ANG-2 transgenic mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: qPCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C shows reduced Slc2a1 expression.

claim: ANG-2 overexpression dramatically reduces adipose tissue hypoxia as judged by decreased pimonidazole-positive signal.
source: In parallel, we also performed pimonidazole staining in sWAT of ANG-2 transgenic mice, to further validate that ANG-2 overexpression dramatically reduces AT hypoxia, as judged by decreased pimonidazole-positive signal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Pimonidazole staining in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D shows reduced hypoxia.

claim: Adipo-ANG2 transgenic mice weigh less than control mice after 5 weeks of HFD/Dox diet.
source: Both the Adipo-ANG2 and Adipo-rtTA mice were challenged with a HFD/Dox diet for five weeks. During this period, body weights were continuously monitored. Adipo-ANG2 transgenic mice weigh less than control mice (Figure 3A).
evidence: Body weight measurements shown in Figure 3A demonstrate lower weight in transgenic mice.

claim: The reduced body weight in Adipo-ANG2 mice is due to a significant decrease in fat mass and increased lean mass.
source: The reduced body weight is due to a significant decrease in fat mass and increased lean mass (Figure 3B).
evidence: Body composition data in Figure 3B shows changes in fat and lean mass.

claim: ANG-2 overexpression significantly improves glucose clearance as judged by oral glucose tolerance tests.
source: Oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTTs) reveal that ANG-2 overexpression significantly improves glucose clearance (Figure 3C).
evidence: OGTT data in Figure 3C demonstrates improved glucose tolerance.

claim: Improved insulin sensitivity is observed in Adipo-ANG2 transgenic mice as judged by insulin tolerance tests.
source: Improved insulin sensitivity is also observed in the Adipo-ANG2 transgenic mice, as judged by insulin tolerance tests (ITT) (Figure 3D).
evidence: ITT data in Figure 3D shows improved insulin sensitivity.

claim: ANG-2 overexpression leads to an improvement of insulin signaling in sWAT, reflected by increased phosphorylated Akt upon insulin stimulation.
source: Consistent with the ITT results, we also demonstrate that ANG-2 overexpression leads to an improvement of insulin signaling in sWAT, reflected by an increased level of phosphorylated Akt upon insulin stimulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 shows increased pAkt.

claim: Both oxygen consumption (VO2) and carbon dioxide generation (VCO2) are significantly enhanced in ANG-2 transgenic mice during light and dark cycles.
source: Both oxygen consumption (VO2) and carbon dioxide generation (VCO2) for the ANG-2 transgenic mice were significantly enhanced during light and dark cycles, reflecting higher energy expenditure upon ANG-2 overexpression (Figure 3E).
evidence: Metabolic cage data in Figure 3E shows increased VO2 and VCO2.

claim: There is no change in the respiratory exchange ratio (RER) between Adipo-ANG2 and control genotypes.
source: However, there is no change in the respiratory exchange ratio (RER) between genotypes (data not shown).
evidence: The manuscript states that RER was measured but showed no difference.

claim: Serum non-esterified free fatty acids (NEFAs) and cholesterol levels are significantly decreased in Adipo-ANG2 mice.
source: The serum lipid profile (Figure 3F) shows that both non-esterified free fatty acids (NEFAs) and cholesterol levels were significantly decreased in Adipo-ANG2 mice, while serum triglycerides only showed a trend towards a decrease.
evidence: Serum lipid measurements in Figure 3F show decreased NEFAs and cholesterol.

claim: Serum triglycerides only showed a trend towards a decrease in Adipo-ANG2 mice.
source: The serum lipid profile (Figure 3F) shows that both non-esterified free fatty acids (NEFAs) and cholesterol levels were significantly decreased in Adipo-ANG2 mice, while serum triglycerides only showed a trend towards a decrease.
evidence: Serum lipid measurements in Figure 3F show a non-significant trend for triglycerides.

claim: Adipo-ANG2 transgenic mice display significantly higher efficiency in lipid clearance after oral lipid gavage.
source: Upon further evaluation with an oral lipid gavage, it is apparent that Adipo-ANG2 transgenic mice display significantly higher efficiency in lipid clearance (Figure 3G).
evidence: Lipid clearance data in Figure 3G demonstrates improved lipid disposal.

claim: Lipoprotein lipase (LPL) activity is significantly enhanced both systemically and locally in Adipo-ANG2 mice.
source: These improvements in lipid metabolism are in part due to a significantly enhanced lipoprotein lipase (LPL) activity, both systemically and locally (Figure 3H).
evidence: LPL activity assay data in Figure 3H shows increased activity.

claim: In sWAT of ANG-2 transgenic mice, mRNA levels of Angptl3 and Angptl8 are significantly reduced.
source: We observe that in sWAT of ANG-2 transgenic mice, mRNA levels of Angptl3 and Angptl8 are significantly reduced, while Angptl4 merely shows a trend toward reduction (Figure 3I).
evidence: qPCR data in Figure 3I shows decreased Angptl3 and Angptl8 expression.

claim: Angptl4 mRNA shows a trend toward reduction in sWAT of ANG-2 transgenic mice.
source: We observe that in sWAT of ANG-2 transgenic mice, mRNA levels of Angptl3 and Angptl8 are significantly reduced, while Angptl4 merely shows a trend toward reduction (Figure 3I).
evidence: qPCR data in Figure 3I shows a non-significant trend for Angptl4.

claim: ANG-2 overexpression results in a dramatic reduction in liver steatosis with much less lipid accumulating in the livers of Adipo-ANG2 mice.
source: Of note, this improved lipid metabolism results in a dramatic reduction in liver steatosis, with much less lipid accumulating in the livers of Adipo-ANG2 mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: H&E staining of liver in Figure 4B shows reduced lipid accumulation.

claim: Plasma adiponectin levels are significantly up-regulated in Adipo-ANG2 mice compared to Adipo-rtTA mice.
source: Compared to Adipo-rtTA mice, the plasma adiponectin levels are significantly up-regulated in Adipo-ANG2 mice (Figure 3J).
evidence: Western blot of plasma in Figure 3J shows increased adiponectin.

claim: Pre-induction of ANG-2 prior to HFD exposure prevents mice from gaining body weight upon HFD exposure.
source: In Figure 3—figure supplement 2, we demonstrate that the pre-induction of ANG-2 prior to HFD exposure prevents the mice from gaining body weight upon HFD exposure, and it also prevents glucose intolerance.
evidence: Body weight and glucose tolerance data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 show preventive effects.

claim: Pre-induction of ANG-2 prevents glucose intolerance upon HFD exposure, particularly evident on day 3.
source: In Figure 3—figure supplement 2, we demonstrate that the pre-induction of ANG-2 prior to HFD exposure prevents the mice from gaining body weight upon HFD exposure, and it also prevents glucose intolerance. This is particularly evident on day 3, when we observe the most dramatic improvements in glucose tolerance.
evidence: OGTT data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 shows improved glucose tolerance on day 3.

claim: By day 7 after HFD exposure, the beneficial effects of ANG-2 pre-induction start to disappear.
source: By day 7, the beneficial effects start to disappear, suggesting that ongoing higher level expression of ANG-2 is required.
evidence: The manuscript reports that beneficial effects diminish by day 7.

claim: H&E staining of sWAT suggests healthier adipose tissue expansion in Adipo-ANG2 mice with significantly smaller average adipocyte size.
source: Overall, H&E staining of sWAT suggests healthier AT expansion in Adipo-ANG2 mice, with significantly smaller average adipocyte size (Figure 4A).
evidence: Histological analysis in Figure 4A shows smaller adipocytes.

claim: Pro-inflammatory macrophage markers including Ly6c1, Tnfa and Nos2 are substantially decreased in sWAT of Adipo-ANG2 mice.
source: Although general inflammatory and macrophage markers, such as Adgre1 (gene symbol for F4/80), Il6 and Csf1r (gene name for CD115), remain relatively unchanged, pro-inflammatory macrophage markers including Ly6c1, Tnfa and Nos2 are substantially decreased; in contrast, the anti-inflammatory macrophage marker Clec10a (gene name for CD301) is significantly upregulated.
evidence: qPCR data shows decreased pro-inflammatory markers.

claim: The anti-inflammatory macrophage marker Clec10a (CD301) is significantly upregulated in sWAT of Adipo-ANG2 mice.
source: Although general inflammatory and macrophage markers, such as Adgre1 (gene symbol for F4/80), Il6 and Csf1r (gene name for CD115), remain relatively unchanged, pro-inflammatory macrophage markers including Ly6c1, Tnfa and Nos2 are substantially decreased; in contrast, the anti-inflammatory macrophage marker Clec10a (gene name for CD301) is significantly upregulated.
evidence: qPCR data shows increased anti-inflammatory marker.

claim: ANG-2 overexpression significantly reduces the number of crown-like structures in eWAT.
source: Consistent with observations in sWAT, we show that ANG-2 overexpression significantly reduces the number of crown like structures and also induces an increase in anti-inflammatory macrophage markers in eWAT (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Histological analysis in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 shows reduced crown-like structures.

claim: ANG-2 overexpression induces an increase in anti-inflammatory macrophage markers in eWAT.
source: Consistent with observations in sWAT, we show that ANG-2 overexpression significantly reduces the number of crown like structures and also induces an increase in anti-inflammatory macrophage markers in eWAT (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: qPCR data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 shows increased anti-inflammatory markers.

claim: Flow cytometry analysis demonstrates a dramatic increase in the percentage of anti-inflammatory macrophages in both sWAT and eWAT of Adipo-ANG2 mice.
source: Furthermore, flow cytometry analysis validates that there is a dramatic increase in the percentage of anti-inflammatory macrophages in both sWAT and eWAT (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 2 shows increased M2 macrophages.

claim: Adipose tissue shows a decrease in collagen accumulation in Adipo-ANG2 mice as demonstrated by trichrome staining.
source: We also noticed that the AT shows a decrease in collagen accumulation, as demonstrated by trichrome staining, and a significant down-regulation in fibrotic gene expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), suggesting that along with the anti-inflammatory changes, a potent anti-fibrotic phenotype is also apparent upon ANG-2 overexpression.
evidence: Trichrome staining in Figure 4—figure supplement 3 shows reduced collagen.

claim: Fibrotic gene expression is significantly down-regulated in adipose tissue of Adipo-ANG2 mice.
source: We also noticed that the AT shows a decrease in collagen accumulation, as demonstrated by trichrome staining, and a significant down-regulation in fibrotic gene expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), suggesting that along with the anti-inflammatory changes, a potent anti-fibrotic phenotype is also apparent upon ANG-2 overexpression.
evidence: qPCR data in Figure 4—figure supplement 3 shows decreased fibrotic gene expression.

claim: ANG-2 induction only marginally increases Evan's Blue leakage in sWAT, suggesting that increased vascular permeability is not a significant issue in ANG-2 overexpressing mice.
source: In contrast to the effects of VEGF-A, ANG-2 induction only marginally increases Evan's Blue leakage in sWAT (Figure 4G). This suggests that increased vascular permeability is not a significant issue in ANG-2 overexpressing mice.
evidence: Evan's Blue staining in Figure 4G shows minimal vascular leakage.

claim: Neither sWAT nor eWAT in Adipo-ANG2 mice show elevated levels of the beiging marker Ucp1 compared to control mice.
source: Neither sWAT nor eWAT in Adipo-ANG2 mice show elevated levels of the beiging marker uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1) compared to control mice (Figure 4H).
evidence: qPCR data in Figure 4H shows no change in Ucp1 expression in WAT.

claim: Both Vegfa and Ucp1 gene expressions are elevated in BAT of ANG-2 transgenic mice.
source: However, upon careful analysis of the BAT in the ANG-2 transgenic mice, we found that both Vegfa and Ucp1 gene expressions are elevated (Figure 4—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: qPCR data in Figure 4—figure supplement 4A shows increased Vegfa and Ucp1 in BAT.

claim: Control mice show bigger lipid droplet accumulation and a more pronounced 'whitening' phenotype in BAT, while ANG-2 overexpressing mice maintain classical BAT histological features under HFD challenge.
source: Based on H&E staining of BAT sections (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B), control mice show a bigger lipid droplet accumulation and a more pronounced 'whitening' phenotype, while ANG-2 overexpressing mice maintain classical BAT histological features.
evidence: H&E staining in Figure 4—figure supplement 4B shows differences in BAT morphology.

claim: Endothelial cell markers Pecam1 and Tek are significantly down-regulated in sWAT of anti-ANG2 antibody-treated mice compared with control IgG administrated mice after 5 weeks of HFD feeding.
source: After 5-week ANG-2 antibody injections (4 µg/g body weight, twice/week, anti-ANG2) along with HFD feeding, endothelial cell markers Pecam1 and Tek in sWAT were quantitated by qPCR. Both markers are shown to be significantly down-regulated in the anti-ANG2 antibody-treated mice, when compared with control IgG administrated mice (Figure 5A).
evidence: qPCR data in Figure 5A shows decreased endothelial markers.

claim: ANG-2 neutralization causes dramatically impaired vascular density in sWAT as judged by reduced endomucin-positive areas.
source: In addition, immunostaining with antibodies against the blood vessel marker endomucin further validates that ANG-2 neutralization prompts dramatically impaired vascular density as judged by reduced endomucin-positive areas (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: Immunostaining and quantification in Figures 5B and C show reduced vascular density.

claim: In sWAT of anti-ANG2 antibody-treated mice, the adipocyte size is slightly larger as judged by H&E staining.
source: We noticed that in sWAT of anti-ANG2 antibody-treated mice, the adipocyte size is slightly larger as judged by H&E staining (Figure 6A).
evidence: H&E staining in Figure 6A shows larger adipocytes.

claim: Significantly higher levels of fibrosis are observed in sWAT of anti-ANG2 antibody-treated mice as judged by trichrome staining.
source: In addition, significantly higher levels of fibrosis are observed as judged by trichrome staining (Figure 6B).
evidence: Trichrome staining in Figure 6B shows increased fibrosis.

claim: In anti-ANG2 antibody injected mice, general inflammatory markers including Il6 and Adgre1 are elevated in sWAT.
source: Further assessment by qPCR shows that in anti-ANG2 antibody injected mice, general inflammatory markers, including Il6 and Adgre1, are elevated.
evidence: qPCR data shows increased inflammatory markers.

claim: Fibrotic mediators such as Tgfb1, Col1a1 and Col6a1 are upregulated in sWAT of anti-ANG2 antibody-treated mice.
source: The upregulation can be observed for fibrotic mediators as well, such as Tgfb1, Col1a1 and Col6a1 (Figure 6D).
evidence: qPCR data in Figure 6D shows increased fibrotic markers.

claim: All pro-inflammatory macrophage markers tested, including Ifng, Tnfa and Nos2, are significantly induced in sWAT upon ANG-2 neutralization.
source: Importantly, a transition from anti-inflammatory to pro-inflammatory macrophage marker expression is seen in sWAT. All pro-inflammatory macrophage markers tested, including Ifng, Tnfa and Nos2, are significantly induced upon ANG-2 neutralization (Figure 6E).
evidence: qPCR data in Figure 6E shows increased pro-inflammatory markers.

claim: Pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic responses are observed in eWAT of mice exposed to ANG-2 neutralizing antibodies.
source: Notably, the pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic responses were not only observed in sWAT, but also were clearly shown in eWAT of the group exposed to neutralizing antibodies (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Histology and qPCR data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 show inflammatory and fibrotic changes in eWAT.

claim: Anti-ANG2 antibody neutralization causes a decrease in the content of the anti-inflammatory macrophage population in both sWAT and eWAT.
source: In addition, we also utilized flow cytometry analysis to demonstrate that in both sWAT and eWAT, anti-ANG2 antibody neutralization causes a decrease in the content of the anti-inflammatory macrophage population (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 2 shows decreased M2 macrophages.

claim: After 5 weeks of HFD challenge, body weights show no difference between the anti-ANG2 treatment group and the control IgG-treated group.
source: After 5 weeks of a HFD challenge, the body weights show no difference between the anti-ANG2 treatment group and the control IgG-treated group (Figure 7A).
evidence: Body weight data in Figure 7A shows no significant difference.

claim: Both glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity are mildly but significantly diminished by ANG-2 antagonization.
source: However, both glucose tolerance (Figure 7B) and insulin sensitivity (Figure 7C) are mildly, however, significantly diminished by ANG-2 antagonization, as judged by OGTTs and ITTs, respectively.
evidence: OGTT and ITT data in Figures 7B and 7C show impaired glucose and insulin tolerance.

claim: Slightly decreased Akt phosphorylation after insulin injection in adipose tissue from anti-ANG2 antibody-treated mice suggests that ANG-2 neutralization impairs insulin signaling.
source: The slightly decreased Akt phosphorylation after insulin injection in AT from anti-ANG2 antibody-treated mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1) further suggests that ANG-2 neutralization impairs insulin signaling and promotes insulin resistance.
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1 shows decreased pAkt.

claim: An oral lipid gavage study demonstrates significantly impaired lipid clearance in ANG-2 antibody-treated mice.
source: Furthermore, although the serum lipid profile remains unchanged between antibody and control groups (data not shown), an oral lipid gavage study demonstrates significantly impaired lipid clearance in ANG-2 antibody-treated mice (Figure 7D).
evidence: Lipid clearance data in Figure 7D shows impaired lipid disposal.

claim: Impaired lipid disposal in ANG-2 antibody-treated mice is associated with a massive elevation of triglyceride levels in the liver.
source: The impaired lipid disposal is associated with a massive elevation of triglyceride levels in the liver (Figure 7E).
evidence: Liver triglyceride measurements in Figure 7E show increased levels.

claim: H&E staining of liver slides shows higher lipid droplet accumulation in the liver of antibody-treated mice.
source: This is further validated by H and E staining of liver slides (Figure 6C), highlighting higher lipid droplet accumulation in the liver of antibody-treated mice.
evidence: H&E staining in Figure 6C shows increased hepatic lipid accumulation.

claim: Endogenous LPL inhibiting genes Angptl3, Angptl4 and Angptl8 are all elevated after anti-ANG2 antibody treatment.
source: In addition, the endogenous LPL inhibiting genes Angptl3, Angptl4 and Angptl8 are all elevated after anti-ANG2 antibody treatment (Figure 7F), suggesting a likely mechanism for a decrease in LPL activity, thereby leading to impaired lipid clearance upon Ang-2 inactivation.
evidence: qPCR data in Figure 7F shows increased Angptl expression.

claim: ANG-2 neutralization significantly lowers circulating adiponectin levels.
source: Lastly, immunoblotting for plasma adiponectin (Figure 7G) demonstrates that ANG-2 neutralization significantly lowers circulating adiponectin levels, reflecting the systemic metabolic deterioration seen in the ANG-2 neutralizing mice.
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 7G shows decreased plasma adiponectin.

claim: Angiogenesis is the rate-limiting step for healthy adipose tissue expansion.
source: We have previously shown that angiogenesis is the rate-limiting step for healthy AT expansion (Sun et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Enhanced angiogenesis facilitates healthy adipose tissue expansion, associated with enhanced adipogenesis, decreased adipose tissue inflammation and minimized fibrotic damage.
source: Enhanced angiogenesis facilitates healthy AT expansion, associated with enhanced adipogenesis, decreased AT inflammation and minimized fibrotic damage.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Inadequate angiogenesis leads to adipose tissue hypoxia, enlarged adipocyte size, increased inflammation and fibrosis, representing an unhealthy pattern in adipose tissue expansion.
source: In contrast, inadequate angiogenesis leads to AT hypoxia, enlarged adipocyte size, increased inflammation and fibrosis, representing an unhealthy pattern in AT expansion (Sun et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Local overexpression of VEGF-A in white adipose tissue and brown adipose tissue both results in improved vascularization and resistance to high-fat diet-induced metabolic dysfunction.
source: We reported earlier that local overexpression of VEGF-A in white AT (WAT) and brown AT (BAT) both results in improved vascularization and resistance to high-fat diet (HFD)-induced metabolic dysfunction (Sun et al., 2012, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: VEGF-B can lead to enhanced adipose tissue vasculature, thereby exerting beneficial metabolic effects.
source: A recent study also reported that VEGF-B can lead to enhanced AT vasculature, thereby exerting beneficial metabolic effects (Robciuc et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a recent study.

claim: In ob/ob mice, ANG-1 expression is decreased in adipose tissue, while ANG-2 expression is increased.
source: There is evidence suggesting that in ob/ob mice, ANG-1 expression is decreased in AT, while ANG-2 expression is increased (Voros et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: ANG-2 induced by FOXC2 overexpression results in enhanced blood vessel sprouting in white adipose tissue.
source: Other data suggest that ANG-2 induced by FOXC2 overexpression results in enhanced blood vessel sprouting in white AT (Xue et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Under different metabolic conditions such as exercise, cold exposure, HFD feeding and fasting, Angpt2 mRNA levels in adipose tissues are subject to change.
source: Our own data show that under different metabolic conditions, such as exercise, cold exposure, HFD feeding and fasting, Angpt2 mRNA levels in the ATs are also subject to change (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: In humans, a meta-analysis demonstrated an association between angiogenesis and insulin sensitivity, showing that chronic insufficiency in tissue vascularization contributes to insulin resistance.
source: In humans, a meta-analysis demonstrated an association between angiogenesis and insulin sensitivity, showing that a chronic insufficiency in tissue vascularization contributes to insulin resistance (Shungin et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a meta-analysis.

claim: VEGF-A overexpression significantly increases white adipose tissue vascularization and 'beiging', and the associated enhancement of energy expenditure prevents unfavorable metabolic changes upon a HFD challenge.
source: Similarly, we have previously shown that VEGF-A overexpression significantly increases WAT vascularization and 'beiging', and the associated enhancement of energy expenditure prevents the unfavorable metabolic changes upon a HFD challenge (Sun et al., 2012, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: A peptide-functionalized nanoparticle delivering rosiglitazone or PGE2 to the adipose tissue vasculature promotes angiogenesis and causes significant browning of white adipose tissue, triggering reduced weight gain and improvements in insulin sensitivity in diet-induced obese mice.
source: A recent study also showed that a peptide-functionalized nanoparticle delivering rosiglitazone or prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) to the AT vasculature promotes angiogenesis and causes significant browning of WAT, triggering further reduced weight gain and improvements in insulin sensitivity in a diet-induced obese mouse model (Xue et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a recent study.

claim: In contrast to VEGF-A overexpression, ANG-2 induction does not activate a beiging program in white adipose tissue but confers improvements in metabolic homeostasis in a beiging-independent manner.
source: In contrast to the VEGF-A overexpression model, ANG-2 induction does not activate a beiging program in WAT, but confers improvements in metabolic homeostasis in a beiging-independent manner.
evidence: The manuscript compares ANG-2 and VEGF-A effects based on experimental data.

claim: Enhancement of vasculature per se is necessary but not sufficient to facilitate development of beiging.
source: Considering the fact that ANG-2 induces WAT angiogenesis without beiging, we conclude that enhancement of vasculature per se is necessary, but not sufficient to facilitate development of beiging.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: At higher concentrations, enhancing VEGF-A triggers widespread edema formation, a phenomenon not observed with ANG-2 overexpression.
source: Furthermore, at higher concentrations, enhancing VEGF-A also triggers widespread edema formation, a phenomenon we did not observe with ANG-2 overexpression, although a slight increase in vascular permeability was shown.
evidence: The claim compares VEGF-A and ANG-2 effects based on experimental observations.

claim: Angiostatin, endostatin and thalidomide significantly reduce body weight in genetically and diet-induced obese mouse models.
source: Angiostatin, endostatin and thalidomide, which are all angiogenesis inhibitors, significantly reduce body weight in genetically and diet-induced obese mouse models (Rupnick et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: TNP-470, a blocking antibody targeting VEGFR2, has anti-obesity effects in both diet-induced and ob/ob mice.
source: TNP-470, a blocking antibody targeting VEGFR2, also has anti-obesity effects in both diet-induced and ob/ob mice (Bråkenhielm et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Several compounds and natural products with anti-angiogenic properties exert anti-obesity and insulin sensitizing effects.
source: Furthermore, several compounds and natural products with anti-angiogenic properties exert anti-obesity and insulin sensitizing effects (Luo et al., 2016; Klaus et al., 2005; Park et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The paradoxical outcomes of both promoting and suppressing angiogenesis protecting against obesity depend on the stage of adipose tissue expansion and the extent of obesity.
source: Counterintuitively, both promoting and suppressing angiogenesis can protect against obesity and associated insulin resistance; the paradoxical outcomes depend on the stage of AT expansion and the extent of obesity.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on reviewing the literature.

claim: Intervening at late stages of obesity with anti-angiogenic approaches seems to improve metabolic outcomes by 'choking off' large adipocytes that tend to be more inflamed.
source: Intervening at late stages of obesity, 'choking off' large adipocytes that tend to be more inflamed with anti-angiogenic approaches seems to be the major source of the improvements.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on understanding of the literature.

claim: In the early stages of obesity (5-week HFD challenge), enhancing angiogenesis by ANG-2 induction is an effective therapy against diet-induced weight gain and insulin resistance.
source: In our present study, in the early stages of obesity (5-week HFD challenge), enhancing angiogenesis by ANG-2 induction is clearly an effective therapy against diet-induced weight gain and insulin resistance (Figure 8).
evidence: The claim summarizes the experimental findings from the study.

claim: ANG-2 can promote macrophages to produce high levels of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10.
source: In addition, ANG-2 prompts macrophages to produce high levels of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 (Coffelt et al., 2011); ANG-2 can promote macrophage conversion into an anti-inflammatory phenotype, as defined by the induction of IL-10, CD206 and a decrease of IL-6 and TNF-α (Seok et al., 2013; Kurniati et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.
